identity.real_world_identity_notes: Caterham Seven Superlight, the lightweight Duratec-engined Seven. AMS2 does not qualify which Superlight it models; the drive matches the sequential specification rather than the standard six-speed manual.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and no automatic blip, so the driver supplies the downshift blip.
This is a different car from the curated Caterham Academy and Supersport, which are five-speed H-pattern cars. No controls are inherited between them.

The downshift blip is required because a racing sequential of this type engages by dogs rather than synchronisers. The reviewed source names the gearbox but not its engagement, so that is an inference.
AMS2 gives no variant suffix, so the exact Superlight is not established beyond the sequential six-speed the drive observed.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.caterham-superlight.20260814t180424879z-f64dc772 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the Superlight R500 and its gearbox options, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The source states power is transmitted by either the standard six-speed gearbox or the optional Caterham Motorsport engineered sequential transmission, and the live drive selected six gears through a sequential stick, which is the sequential option.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Lightweight Duratec Seven. AMS2 does not say which Superlight it models, and the drive found the sequential rather than the standard six-speed manual. The car cuts the upshift; the downshift blip is yours.
